mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -8.3% to -3.4% over four weeks, signaling a sustained recovery trend. This momentum will continue, driving RETAIL_REC further positive over the next four weeks as the baseline effect compounds.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 4.9 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains elevated at 40.0% while RETAIL_REC remains suppressed at -3.4%, indicating consumers are prioritizing essential shopping over discretionary retail. When GROCERY_PHARM falls below 35%, discretionary retail will capture released purchasing power, lifting RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM falling below 35%, or GROCERY_PHARM remains above 35% for the entire forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations remain suppressed at -3.1%, constraining foot traffic to retail zones. If TRANSIT mobility recovers to within 2 percentage points of baseline, retail accessibility improves and RETAIL_REC will rise by at least 3 percentage points within one week.
failure_condition: TRANSIT rises above -2.0 but RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 3 percentage points within the following week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized around -23% over the last two weeks, indicating outdoor recreation is not substituting for retail. Sustained suppression of PARKS signals that retail-and-recreation venues remain the primary outlet for discretionary activity, supporting RETAIL_REC recovery.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -21.0% shows no recovery trend
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -10% while RETAIL_REC remains below -2%, indicating substitution away from retail venues.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL elevation at 5.7% combined with WORKPLACES suppression at -3.9% indicates home-based activity dominance. When WORKPLACES recovers toward -1% or higher, commuting routines will resume and incidental retail visits during work-day transit will increase RETAIL_REC by 2+ percentage points.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -2.0 but RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 2 percentage points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The four-week trend shows RETAIL_REC improving at a decelerating rate (improvements of 2.6, 2.0, and 0.3 percentage points week-on-week). This deceleration signals saturation of the recovery cycle; RETAIL_REC will stagnate or decline over the next four weeks as the rebound exhausts.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC week-on-week improvements declining from 2.6 to 0.3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both suppressed and stable, indicating persistent mobility restrictions. If both remain below -2% for the next week, retail foot traffic will remain constrained and RETAIL_REC will not recover beyond -2%, failing to reach positive territory.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -2.0 percentage points
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above -2.0 within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -2% despite both remaining suppressed.

This regime persists if GROCERY_PHARM stays above 38% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 5%; under these conditions, RETAIL_REC will decline further as discretionary spending remains suppressed.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains above 38% and RESIDENTIAL remains above 5%
